The same edit left the file's markdown structure broken (dangling code fence) — raised separately as new finding C, unrelated to the type-correctness substance of this finding.

new_findings.summary: Making `status` a required, no-default parameter (the fix for finding 1) leaves the existing `minna start-feature` command with no way to supply it, and no task specifies how this gap is closed — the required smoke test (T016) calls `start-feature` with no `--status` flag and expects it to succeed.
new_findings.evidence: `src/cli.ts:45-57`'s `startFeatureCommand` reads only `--project`/`--title`. `src/core/state.ts:35-52`'s current `startFeature(project, title)` takes no status argument. `contracts/api.md:55`'s `createFeature(actor, id, title, status, options?)` now requires `status` with no default. `contracts/cli.md` documents only `log`/`verify`/`export`, no `--status` flag for `start-feature`. `tasks.md:85-89` (T008) says only to 'delegate to db.ts' and 'map status from projection back to the legacy phase field,' without stating what value `startFeature` will pass as the now-mandatory `status`. Yet `tasks.md:145` (T016 step 2) runs `npm run dev start-feature --project test --title "smoke-validation"` with no `--status` flag and expects a working feature to result. Separately, `plan.md:76`'s read-path mapping ('map database status to legacy phase') cannot type-check as stated either: `types.ts:3-11`'s `PhaseId` is a closed 8-value union and `FeatureState.phase` is typed `PhaseId`, while the journal's `status` is an unconstrained string per spec.md's own design (no enum) — assigning an arbitrary caller status into `phase` either fails to compile, requires an unstated cast, or throws at runtime in `workflow.ts:6-8` (`getCurrentPhase` throws on any value not present in `workflow.phases`).
new_findings.recommendation: Specify, in tasks.md and contracts/cli.md, exactly what status value `start-feature` supplies to `createFeature` (a new `--status` flag, or a stated default chosen at the CLI/state.ts layer, explicitly documented as such rather than silently hardcoded) and how `state.ts`'s read-path mapping turns an arbitrary `status` string into a valid `PhaseId` for `workflow.ts` (e.g. treat any unrecognized status as a specific fallback phase, and say so in the plan).

new_findings.summary: The plan-review gate checklist itself still reads FAIL and still shows CHK001 and CHK009 unchecked, despite the producer's response report claiming both are addressed.
new_findings.evidence: checklists/plan-review.md:7 states `**Gate result**: FAIL — open: CHK001, CHK009 (2026-07-16)`, and lines 11 and 25 still show `- [ ] **CHK001**` and `- [ ] **CHK009**` (unchecked), not `- [x]`. The producer's response report items 7-8 claim both are 'Status: addressed.' By this checklist's own stated purpose ('Verification gate to check the plan and design artifacts... before any implementation code is written'), the artifact currently under review still formally reports a failed gate.
new_findings.recommendation: Update checklists/plan-review.md to check off CHK001/CHK009 and correct the Gate result line once the corresponding fixes are independently confirmed (this is the Codex/requirements re-review's item to verify, but the file should not be left self-contradictory in the meantime).

new_findings.summary: contracts/api.md lost its title, intro, and '## 1. Type Definitions' header plus the opening ` ```typescript ` fence when the source-of-truth note was added, but the original closing ``` ``` ``` fence (now line 24) was left in place with no matching opening fence.
new_findings.evidence: api.md:1 now opens directly with a `// Note: ...` comment followed immediately by TypeScript code (lines 3-23), with a lone ` ``` ` at line 24 and no ` ```typescript ` (or any) opening fence anywhere above it. Markdown renderers will not treat lines 1-23 as a code block, and the stray closing fence will corrupt rendering of whatever follows.
new_findings.recommendation: Restore an opening ` ```typescript ` fence before the type definitions (with or without restoring the removed header/title), so the closing fence at line 24 has a matching pair.

new_findings.summary: `WriteOptions.faultInjection` is exposed as a plain optional parameter on every production write function (`recordEvent`, `createFeature`, `updateFeatureStatus`), not as a test-only seam, so any caller can pass `{ faultInjection: true }` to deliberately defeat the same-transaction guarantee Constitution III relies on.
new_findings.evidence: api.md:5-7 defines `WriteOptions { faultInjection?: boolean }`, and this same type is the `options` parameter on `recordEvent` (api.md:40), `createFeature` (api.md:55), and `updateFeatureStatus` (api.md:67) — the actual production write API, with no stated restriction to test builds or a separate test-only entry point.
new_findings.recommendation: Move the fault-injection hook out of the public production API surface (e.g. dependency-inject a transaction runner that tests can substitute, or expose a separate `_test`-prefixed export) so no production call site can pass a flag that intentionally corrupts a transaction.

new_findings.summary: The Phase Summary Table's Phase 03 row still reads 'T011 - T015,' left over from before the old T010 (workflow.ts task) was deleted and subsequent tasks renumbered; the actual Phase 03 section now spans T010-T015.

new_findings.summary: The `features` table DDL comment still says the `status` column has a 'default: specify,' contradicting the payload contract and fold logic three sections below it in the same document, which now require `status` as caller-supplied with no default.
new_findings.evidence: data-model.md:31: `status TEXT NOT NULL,             -- Current generic status string (default: 'specify')`. No `DEFAULT` clause actually exists in the SQL, and data-model.md:52, 60, and 101 all now show `status` as a required, caller-supplied field with no fallback — the comment is stale and self-contradictory within the same file.
new_findings.recommendation: Remove '(default: 'specify')' from the DDL comment, or replace it with 'required, caller-supplied, no default' to match the rest of the document.
